name: Neziah
overview: Neziah was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role, as noted in Ezra 2:54, places him within the Levitical community dedicated to the service of the temple. There are no additional notes recorded about his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Neziah means 'director [of worship],' reflecting a role connected to temple service or leadership in worship. This meaning aligns with his function as a temple servant mentioned in Scripture, specifically in Ezra 2:54.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Neziah as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical heritage. Beyond this tribal relationship, no other family connections or relationships are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Neziah's significance lies in his representation of the faithful Levitical servants who returned from exile and resumed temple duties. His mention in Ezra 2:54 highlights the restoration of temple worship and the continuity of Levitical service in the post-exilic community. As a temple servant, Neziah exemplifies the dedication required to maintain the worship of God according to the Law.
